A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same 29-page paper, Token-Efficient Change Detection in LLM APIs, including Appendices A–D. Full-text comparison and rendering establish that differences are confined to first-page date/version markings; pages 2–29 are pixel-identical.

before.justification: v1 reports original TinyChange experiments, commercial-API border-input prevalence measurements, and 23-day monitoring results in Section 5, with supplementary experimental results in Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains the original TinyChange experiments, commercial-API prevalence measurements, and monitoring results in Section 5 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithms 1–2 retain identical border-input discovery, reference sampling, and support-mismatch detection procedures. The experimental TV-distance statistic is also unchanged.

E1.justification: The nine-model TinyChange evaluation, fine-tuning/pruning/noise perturbation coverage, and commercial-API populations listed in Appendix D are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain MET, MMLU-ALG, and grey-box LT, including the same temperature variants of MET and MMLU-ALG in Figures 2 and 6.

E3.justification: Sections 5 and D.5–D.6 retain identical sampling budgets, temperature settings, parameter sweeps, ROC AUC evaluation, and cost calculations. The selected B3IT configuration remains five prompts, 50 reference samples, and three detection samples per prompt.

E4.justification: Prompt/sample sensitivity sweeps, temperature-dependent border-input prevalence, and perturbation-difficulty analyses are unchanged in Figures 1, 3, 4, 6, and 7.

E5.justification: Appendix D.5 retains the same 1,000 generated test statistics and 250 bootstraps, with 95% confidence intervals for Figures 3 and 7. No uncertainty-reporting or repeated-run information changes.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are unchanged. For example, Section 5.1.3 still reports B3IT ROC AUC 0.9 at $2.2/year, and Section 5.2.3 still identifies eight persistent endpoint changes.

T1.justification: The LAN analysis, phase-transition theorem, support-test error bounds, and optimality result in Sections 3–4 are identical. Appendices A–C retain all definitions, proofs, and sampling-budget derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about black-box B3IT, low-temperature sensitivity, performance comparable to grey-box methods, and a 30-fold cost advantage.

C2.justification: Explanations involving floating-point precision and inference nondeterminism, limitations for reasoning endpoints and larger supports, and interpretations of detected API changes are unchanged.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, pseudocode, model/endpoint lists, prompt-construction instructions, experimental details, and OLMo workaround are identical. No technical or resource-access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 6, citations throughout the paper, and the reference list are unchanged, preserving the same positioning relative to change detection, inference nondeterminism, and LLM fingerprinting.

P1.justification: The first-page preprint date changes from February 12, 2026 to May 5, 2026, and the arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated February 11 to v2 dated May 4. The prose, terminology, and document structure otherwise remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–7, Algorithms 1–2, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendering confirms identical pages 2–29; first-page differences only reflect the updated date/version text.

improvement.justification: v2 updates only first-page date/version markings. The scientific content, empirical evidence, proofs, limitations, reproducibility information, and substantive presentation remain identical, including the appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
